title: Normalized sheaf insertion calculus at an automorphic point
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $h:s\xrightarrow{\sim}s$ a scheme automorphism, and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Use compatible small skeletons of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], its constant ring sheaf $A_s$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and the category $\mathcal M$ of $A_s$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $r\geq1$ let $H_r=(h^r)^*$ be ordinary module pullback: inverse image followed by extension of scalars along the canonical constant-section-preserving map $c^{h^r}_A$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Put $(R_rF)(U\xrightarrow{u}s)=F(U\xrightarrow{h^ru}s)$, with the restrictions of $F$ and the constant-coefficient action transported through $c^{h^r}_A$.

For $F\in\mathcal M$ define the $A$-module map $j_{r,F}:F(s,\operatorname{id})\to(H_rF)(s,\operatorname{id})$ by restriction along $h^r:(s,h^r)\to(s,\operatorname{id})$, the inverse-image colimit coprojection at $(s,h^r)$ with graph $(\operatorname{id}_s,\operatorname{id}_s):s\to s\times_{s,h^r}s$, its sheafification map [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and the scalar insertion $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. For $m\geq1$ write $T_{m,F}:H_1H_mF\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{m+1}F$ for the ordinary canonical module-pullback compositor, oriented from successive pullback to direct pullback.

There are $A_s$-linear isomorphisms $e_{r,F}:H_rF\xrightarrow{\sim}R_rF$, natural in $F$ and in site objects. They have the following normalization: at $U\xrightarrow{u}s$, insertion of $x\in F(U,h^ru)$ at the comma index $(U,h^ru)$ with graph $(u,\operatorname{id}_U):U\to s\times_{s,h^r}U$, followed by sheafification and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, maps to $x$. With the identification $R_1R_mF=R_{m+1}F$ induced by $h^mh=h^{m+1}$, they satisfy
$$e_{m+1,F}\circ T_{m,F}=R_1(e_{m,F})\circ e_{1,H_mF},\qquad e_{r,F}(s)\circ j_{r,F}=\operatorname{res}_{h^r}^{F}.$$
For every $A_s$-module morphism $v:F\to G$,
$$ (H_rv)(s)\circ j_{r,F}=j_{r,G}\circ v(s),\qquad
j_{m+1,F}=T_{m,F}(s)\circ j_{1,H_mF}\circ j_{m,F}.$$
For every cochain complex $K$ of $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the degreewise maps $j_{r,K^i}$ form an $A$-linear chain map $j_{r,K}:\Gamma(s,K)\to\Gamma(s,C(H_r)K)$, natural for chain maps, and the last composition identity holds as an equality of chain maps with $T_m$ applied degreewise. Here $C(H_r)$ denotes termwise application of $H_r$ and $\Gamma(s,K)^i=K^i(s,\operatorname{id})$.

proof.text: Fix $r\geq1$ and put $f=h^r$. Since $f$ is an isomorphism, [lem-weil-iso-weakly-etale] makes $(s,f)$ an object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] with $X=W=s$ and $W\to X=f$. Write $P_r=f^{-1}$ on underlying abelian sheaves. It gives a natural isomorphism $p_{r,F}:R_rF\xrightarrow{\sim}P_rF$ of abelian sheaves: at $(U,u)$ it sends $x\in F(U,fu)$ to the coprojection indexed by $(U,fu)$ with graph $(u,\mathrm{id}_U)$, followed by sheafification. This also applies to ring sheaves and their module actions. The same lemma identifies $R_rA_s\to P_rA_s\xrightarrow{c^f_A}A_s$ with the constant-section-preserving restriction comparison. Thus the scalar transport on $R_rF$ in the statement is exactly the one belonging to this $p_{r,F}$. The isomorphisms are natural both in $F$ and in all restriction maps; no evaluation-exactness or constructibility hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; its graph-index restriction specialization

proof.text: By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], the specified $c^f_A:P_rA_s\to A_s$ is an isomorphism, not a separately chosen coefficient identification. Apply [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso] with $R=P_rA_s$, $S=A_s$ and $M=P_rF$. Its normalized comparison, followed by $p_{r,F}^{-1}$ from step 1, gives $e_{r,F}:H_rF\xrightarrow{\sim}R_rF$. Explicitly, on the sheafification image of a pure tensor $y\otimes a$ it is $p_{r,F}^{-1}((c^f_A)^{-1}(a)y)$. The inverse, denoted $\rho_{r,F}$, sends $x\in R_rF(U)$ to the sheafification image of $p_{r,F}(x)\otimes1$. The cited tensor comparison is natural and linear, so $e$ is natural in modules and site objects and is $A_s$-linear for the action in step 1. Substitution of $y=p_{r,F}(x)$ and $a=1$ proves precisely the requested graph-insertion normalization.

proof.text: Write $a_{1,m}:h^{-1}(h^m)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(h^{m+1})^{-1}$ for the adjunction-compatible sheaf compositor. The same-unit lemma [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition], with its $h=h$ and $k=h^m$, gives $c^{h^{m+1}}_A\circ a_{1,m,A_s}=c^h_A\circ h^{-1}(c^{h^m}_A)$; its displayed $\alpha$ is $a_{1,m}^{-1}$. Hence the coefficients satisfy exactly the hypothesis of [lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit]. That theorem identifies the actual canonical module compositor $T_{m,F}$ with the explicit tensor comparison formed from $a_{1,m}$ and scalar multiplication. In particular nested scalar units go to the direct scalar unit, since its formula $(y\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto y\otimes c^h_A(a)b$ sends $(y\otimes1)\otimes1$ to $y\otimes1$. This fixes the orientation as $H_1H_m\to H_{m+1}$, with no freedom to choose another isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites; normalized module comparison as in sites-modules.tex Tag 03D3

proof.text:
At $(U,u)$ take $x\in F(U,h^{m+1}u)$. First $R_1(\rho_{m,F})$ inserts it at $(U,h^{m+1}u)$ with graph $(hu,\mathrm{id}_U)$; then $\rho_{1,H_mF}$ inserts the resulting section with graph $(u,\mathrm{id}_U)$. The formula of [lem-trf-site-inverse-image-composition-generators], applied to the base-change functors $B_{h^m}$ followed by $B_h$, sends these nested abelian coprojections to their composite graph. In the iterated fibre product its three coordinates are $(u,hu,\mathrm{id}_U)$; the canonical map to $s\times_{s,h^{m+1}}U$ retains the first and last coordinates, so its graph is $(u,\mathrm{id}_U)$, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The tensor formula identified in step 3 by [lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit] sends both scalar units to the scalar unit. Therefore, for every such $x$,
$$T_{m,F}\circ\rho_{1,H_mF}\circ R_1(\rho_{m,F})(x)=\rho_{m+1,F}(x).$$
These are maps with source $R_1R_mF=R_{m+1}F$, so testing every section on every object proves equality of sheaf maps. Composing with the inverse isomorphisms gives $e_{m+1,F}\circ T_{m,F}=R_1(e_{m,F})\circ e_{1,H_mF}$. This argument does not assume arbitrary sections of a sheafification are single colimit representatives: its source sections are the actual $x\in F(U,h^{m+1}u)$.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites, on nested coprojections; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D3 for tensor units

proof.text:
At the final object $(s,\mathrm{id})$, $\rho_{r,F}(s)$ is insertion at $(s,h^r)$ with graph $(\mathrm{id}_s,\mathrm{id}_s)$ followed by the tensor unit. Thus the definition of $j$ is exactly
$$j_{r,F}=\rho_{r,F}(s)\circ\operatorname{res}_{h^r}^F,$$
which gives $e_{r,F}(s)j_{r,F}=\operatorname{res}_{h^r}^F$. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction and a module morphism commute; restriction is $A$-linear through constant sections, since constants restrict to the same constants [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Step 2 makes $\rho(s)$ linear as well. For $v:F\to G$, naturality of $\rho$ and the restriction square give
$$(H_rv)(s)j_{r,F}=\rho_{r,G}(s)(R_rv)(s)\operatorname{res}_{h^r}^F=\rho_{r,G}(s)\operatorname{res}_{h^r}^Gv(s)=j_{r,G}v(s).$$

source.place: Tag 06UM, section-pullback; explicit restriction/insertion formula and naturality

proof.text:
To prove the composition law, apply the isomorphism $e_{m+1,F}(s)$ to its proposed right side. Step 4 followed by step 5 for the module $H_mF$ gives
$$e_{m+1,F}(s)T_{m,F}(s)j_{1,H_mF}j_{m,F}=e_{m,F}(s,h)\operatorname{res}^{H_mF}_{h}j_{m,F}.$$
Naturality of $e_{m,F}$ in the site arrow $h:(s,h)\to(s,\mathrm{id})$ changes this to
$$\operatorname{res}^{R_mF}_{h}\,e_{m,F}(s)j_{m,F}=\operatorname{res}^{R_mF}_{h}\operatorname{res}^{F}_{h^m}.$$
The first restriction here is $F$'s restriction along $h:(s,h^{m+1})\to(s,h^m)$. Presheaf functoriality, part of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], identifies the composite with $\operatorname{res}^F_{h^mh}=\operatorname{res}^F_{h^{m+1}}=e_{m+1,F}(s)j_{m+1,F}$. Cancelling $e_{m+1,F}(s)$ proves the stated equality. All maps have source $F(s,\mathrm{id})$ and target $(H_{m+1}F)(s,\mathrm{id})$.

source.place: Tag 06UM, section-pullback; composition of restrictions under the normalized compositor

proof.text:
Use cochain complexes and chain maps as defined in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The natural comparison with $R_r$ from step 2 shows $H_r$ is additive: after conjugating by $e$, its action on a sum of maps is the sum of their restrictions. Hence $C(H_r)K$ is a complex. Apply step 5 with $v=d_K^i:K^i\to K^{i+1}$; it gives
$$(H_rd_K^i)(s)j_{r,K^i}=j_{r,K^{i+1}}d_K^i(s),$$
exactly the chain-map equation for the degreewise $A$-linear maps $j_{r,K^i}$. Applying the same equality to each component of a chain map $K\to L$ proves naturality on complexes. The naturality of $T_m$ in step 3 similarly makes its degreewise components a chain isomorphism. Finally step 6 in each degree is the required composition identity of chain maps, since chain maps are equal when all their components agree. No derived localization or boundedness argument is involved.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q64-2337ebdd6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and the mathematics holds. It is one commit with the item and the report, a first split with no new nodes and no repair note. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live, so it is not superseded, and it is not on the dropped list. The statement is byte-identical to live, including Q96's added sheafification citation. The 7 steps total 6311 characters and contain all of Q96's old parent Steps 2-5 with more detail. The dependency closure (275 nodes) does not reach the item, so there is no cycle. Step 1: lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction (1)-(3) applies with X=W=s and r=h^r, since an isomorphism is weakly étale (Mathlib leaf). G|_W(U,u)=F(U,h^r u) is R_rF, and the initial index is (U,h^r u) with graph (u,id_U). Step 2: lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso applies with R=P_rA_s, S=A_s and c=c^{h^r}_A, which is invertible by prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map. Its inverse m↦η(m⊗1) gives the stated normalization. Step 3: lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition with h and k=h^m gives exactly the definition of c_{kh} in lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit, because α=a^{-1} by uniqueness of the adjunction-compatible comparison. So that lemma's (kh)^* is H_{m+1}, and t_{h,k} is T_m in the direction H_1H_m→H_{m+1}. Step 4: I recomputed the nested graphs. ψ=(hu,id) into s×_{h^m}U and φ=(u,id) into s×_hU give u(ψ)φ=(u,hu,id_U). The q of def-pc-fibre-product sends this to (u,id_U), which is the index of ρ_{m+1}. The tensor formula sends (y⊗1)⊗1 to y⊗1. Equality is tested on every section x of the source, so no single-representative assumption is used. Steps 5-7 are elementary and I checked them with typed domains: e_r(s)j_r=res_{h^r}; then e_m(s,h)res_h=res^{R_mF}_h e_m(s), and res^F along (s,h^{m+1})→(s,h^m) composed with res_{h^m} is res_{h^{m+1}}; the chain-map clauses hold degreewise, with additivity coming through e. Edge cases checked: h=id, m=1, U empty, F=0 and F=A_s. Stacks tags 03CE, 03CB, 06UM, 03CZ and 03D3 were checked against tags/tags and sites.tex:6094. No SGA is cited. Not duplicates: lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural (r=1 only), lem-trf-point-system-power-roos-coherence (integral systems) and lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-powers (integral towers). I accept all five declared tool_uses as generic sheaf, site and coefficient black boxes. Advisory: the statement's 'canonical compositor' T_m names no node, but Step 3 pins it to the unique adjunction-compatible comparison of lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit. No changes.
